cards.explanation: The answer is water, friends. The LORD tells Jeremiah, the prophet, to put the loincloth around his waist, “…but do not let it touch water.” (Jeremiah 13:1) Linen that has to stay away from water. I can't keep flour off my apron for ten minutes, so I'm impressed.

The answer is True. Jeremiah says, “So I bought a loincloth in accordance with the word of the LORD, and I put it around my waist.” (Jeremiah 13:2) Strange orders, and he did it just as the LORD said. I think a lot of us would have at least raised an eyebrow, friends, and I have a LOT of eyebrow.

The answer is the rocks. The LORD says to hide the loincloth “…in a crevice of the rocks.” (Jeremiah 13:4) A crack in the rocks at Perath. Not the back of a junk drawer, where I spent years, and believe me, friends, I know the difference.

The answer is ruined and of no use at all, and that's the whole point. Jeremiah, the prophet, digs it up and finds that “…it was ruined…” (Jeremiah 13:7) It's of no use at all. After many days in the rocks, that loincloth was done. Now we get to hear why the LORD wanted it buried.
The answer is the pride of Judah and Jerusalem. The LORD says, “…I will ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.” (Jeremiah 13:9) The ruined loincloth was a picture of that.

The answer is gods. The LORD says these people “…go after other gods to serve and worship them…” (Jeremiah 13:10) They refuse to listen to His words and follow their own stubborn hearts, too. That's a lot of ways to walk away from Him, friends.

The answer is to be His people for His glory. That's the reason the LORD gives. He made them cling to Him “…so that they might be My people for My renown and praise and glory.” (Jeremiah 13:11) A loincloth stays close to the waist, and He wanted them close to Him. Then the verse says it plainly: “But they did not listen.”

The answer is False, and the verse says so plainly. After the LORD says He made Israel and Judah cling to Him, He adds, “But they did not listen.” (Jeremiah 13:11) That one sentence is a heavy way to end the picture. The loincloth clung, and they didn't hear.

The answer is that they say they surely know that already. The LORD says they will reply, “Don’t we surely know that every wineskin should be filled with wine?” (Jeremiah 13:12) That sounds like the look we've all given somebody explaining the obvious, friends.

The answer is False, and the verse names them. The LORD says He will fill with drunkenness “…all who live in this land—the kings who sit on David’s throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the people of Jerusalem.” (Jeremiah 13:13) The kings and the priests are not spared. This part of the passage is heavy, and nobody is skipped.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “I will allow no mercy or pity or compassion to keep Me from destroying them.” (Jeremiah 13:14) None of those three will stop Him. I think this is a hard verse to sit with, friends, and that's okay.
